## Overview: Forecast the targets!

The "targets" are time-series of data for use in model development and forecast evaluation. They are updated as new data are made available.

The `r nrow(variables)` targets are organised into `r length(groups)` "themes". The themes and links to the target files are included below.

## Where to start {#sec-starting-sites}

If you are just getting started, we recommend the following focal sites for each theme. The first site in the list is the recommended starting site.

```{r results = "asis"}
cat(paste0("-   ", groups, ": ", purrr::map_chr(focal, toString), collapse = "\n"))
```

As you develop your forecasting skills and want to expand to more sites, the targets are available at all `r nrow(sites)` sites. You may also consider submitting forecasts to sites that match your interests. For example, a winter class may be more interested in forecasting southern sites than a summer class, which may focus on more northern sites.

More information about the sites can be found in the [site metadata](`r links$sites`).

## Explore the targets and themes {#sec-targets}

In the tables,

-   "duration" is the time-step of the variable, where `P1D` is a daily mean and `P1W` is a weekly total.
-   the "horizon" is how far ahead we want you to forecast.
-   the "latency" is the time between data collection and data availability in the target file.

```{r results = "asis"}
md <- function(df) paste(knitr::kable(df, format = "pipe"), collapse = "\n")

render_tabs(purrr::map(groups, function(group) {
  url <- cfg$target_groups[[group]]$targets_file
  prose_file <- file.path("_content", "targets", paste0(group, ".md"))
  prose <- if (file.exists(prose_file)) readLines(prose_file) else character()
  table <- variables |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$group == !!group) |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c("variable", "duration", "description",
                                  "horizon", "Latency"))) |>
    dplyr::rename_with(tolower)
  if (is.null(url)) {
    return(list(title = group, text = c(prose, "", md(table)), widget = NULL))
  }
  targets <- readr::read_csv(targets_files(cfg, url), show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
  # The time series are drawn in the browser (js/pages/targets.js) from the
  # staged data, like the forecasts on the explorer.
  chart <- paste0('<div data-targets-group="', group, '"></div>')
  list(
    title = group,
    text = c(prose, "", md(table), "",
             "The target file is at the following URL:", "",
             paste0("[`", url, "`](", url, ")"), "",
             "Read it with the code below (the same as on the [Data](data.html) page):", "",
             # The code is drawn in the browser (js/snippets.js), as on the Data page:
             # open buckets are read directly, private ones with a key from the environment.
             paste0('<div data-read-targets data-url="', gsub('"', "&quot;", url, fixed = TRUE), '"></div>'),
             "",
             "The file contains the following columns:", "",
             md(utils::head(stats::na.omit(targets))), "",
             "and the time series at the focal sites:", "", chart),
    widget = NULL,
    empty = ""
  )
}))
```

## Explore the sites

```{r}
# Zoomed to fit the sites (a few hundred metres to a few hundred kilometres
# apart, or a continent), not to a fixed view. Nearby markers are clustered
# only when there are many.
many <- nrow(sites) > 20
leaflet::leaflet(sites) |>
  leaflet::fitBounds(min(sites$longitude), min(sites$latitude),
                     max(sites$longitude), max(sites$latitude),
                     options = list(maxZoom = 13, padding = c(40, 40))) |>
  leaflet::addTiles(group = "OSM") |>
  leaflet::addProviderTiles(leaflet::providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "Imagery") |>
  leaflet::addProviderTiles(leaflet::providers$Esri.WorldTopoMap, group = "Topo Map") |>
  leaflet::addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Imagery", "OSM", "Topo Map")) |>
  leaflet::addMarkers(lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude,
                      popup = ~paste0(site_name, " (", site_id, ")"),
                      clusterOptions = if (many) leaflet::markerClusterOptions())
```

<br /> <br /> The following table lists all the sites in the `r cfg$challenge_long_name`. The columns with theme names say whether the site is in that theme's target file.

```{r}
sites |>
  dplyr::select(-latitude, -longitude) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
